name: Qatar
summary: Qatar Central Bank (QCB) licenses and supervises onshore banks, including AML/CFT, customer protection and technology risk, through its Instructions to Banks, circulars and regulations. The Qatar Financial Information Unit receives suspicious transaction reports, the National Counter Terrorism Committee runs targeted financial sanctions, the National Cyber Security Agency administers the personal data law, and the General Tax Authority is CRS competent authority. The Qatar Financial Centre has its own regulator (QFCRA) and is not covered here. No Qatari official site could be opened in this session, so all entries are at most competence pending source checks.

regulators.name: Qatar Central Bank
regulators.role: Licenses, regulates and supervises banks and other financial institutions outside the QFC, including AML/CFT supervision, customer protection and technology risk.

regulators.name: Qatar Financial Information Unit
regulators.role: Receives and analyses suspicious transaction reports and issues reporting instructions and guidance.

regulators.name: National Cyber Security Agency
regulators.role: National cyber security authority; administers the Personal Data Privacy Protection Law and the National Information Assurance standard.

regulators.name: General Tax Authority
regulators.role: Competent authority for the Common Reporting Standard.

regulators.name: Qatar Financial Centre Regulatory Authority
regulators.role: Separate regulator for firms authorised in the Qatar Financial Centre, with its own rules; not covered by the mappings in this file.

programs.title: Qatar | AML/CFT Compliance under Law No. 20 of 2019 and the QCB AML/CFT Instructions
programs.why: Law 20 of 2019 and its Implementing Regulations require banks to run AML/CFT programmes with policies, controls and staff measures; the QCB instructions set the training part. Search extracts of the QCB AML/CFT Instructions describe annual and as-needed training; this would support a mandatory classification once the text is opened. The official texts could not be opened in this session (qcb.gov.qa sends an incomplete TLS certificate chain; qfiu.gov.qa, almeezan.qa and other .qa hosts refuse automated access), so the entry stays at competence.

notes: Law No. 20 of 2019 replaced Law No. 4 of 2010 as the AML/CFT law; Council of Ministers Decision No. 41 of 2019 issued its Implementing Regulations. Decree-Law No. 19 of 2021 amended the law and Cabinet Decision No. 14 of 2021 amended the regulations (per QFIU listings seen in search results).

Secondary sources report a Decree-Law No. 18 of 2025 amending Law 20 of 2019 to set up a national AML/CFT committee at the QCB and an independent FIU. This could not be confirmed against the official gazette.
The QCB AML/CFT Instructions for financial institutions date from May 2020; some secondary sources mention later updates, but no newer official edition was found.
QCB Circular 25/2022 (governance instructions in banks), amended by Circular 2/2023, appears to have replaced the 2015 corporate governance guidelines.
QCB published a regulatory framework for digital banks in December 2024 and an Artificial Intelligence Guideline; neither was opened.
